title: Grief Is A Houseplant with Ronnie Delacroix
description: Late-night advice on Snazzie FM. Ronnie reads heartbroken letters from listeners and answers each one with serene confidence and zero usefulness. Barry tries to be kind. Tonight's prescription for every wound: re-pot it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Good evening, and welcome to the soft hour. This is Grief Is A Houseplant, where you send me your heartbreak, and I send it back, slightly bigger. I'm Ronnie Delacroix.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: And I'm Barry. And I just want to say to anyone writing in tonight... we hear you. This stuff is heavy.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It is heavy, Barry. That's why we re-pot it. <p:0.3> First letter. Maureen, from the cul-de-sac, writes, quote, my husband of forty-one years passed in the spring. The house is unbearably quiet. I keep setting out two coffee cups out of habit, and I don't know how to be one person again. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Oh, Maureen. <p:0.3> Forty-one years. That's a whole life. Ronnie, she just needs to know it's okay to grieve at her own pace...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Two cups, Maureen. That's the issue. You've got a one-cup life and a two-cup kitchen. So we downsize the cups. Get yourself a little radio for the quiet. And honestly? Re-pot the whole thing into a smaller, more manageable apartment.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, she's not a houseplant, she lost her husband...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And the coasters, Maureen. Put the coasters on the LEFT now. Fresh start. You'll feel it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Coaster placement. <p:0.3> She's mourning and you gave her coaster placement.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Solved. Next one. This is Devon, who asked us not to say where he works. Devon writes, quote, I got laid off after eleven years. My whole identity was that job. I cried in a parking garage and I feel like I've just... disappeared. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's a real one. Losing work can feel like losing yourself. Devon, you have not disappeared...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A parking garage, Barry. Right away I'm hearing a parking problem. Were you validated, Devon? Because that's its own grief.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He wasn't talking about parking, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You know who else left? Gary. Co-host, two thousand nine. Walked out mid-segment, never looked back. <p:0.3> So I get it, Devon. People leave you. Anyway, the garage crying? That's great cardio. And then you re-pot the career into a bigger garage. Onward.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That was about Gary. <p:0.3> That whole answer was about Gary.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Healing, Barry. <p:0.3> Letter three. Aisha, from the east side. Quote, my youngest just left for college. The bedrooms are empty. I stood in the doorway of an empty room and I didn't recognize my own life anymore. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Empty nest. Aisha, that ache is love with nowhere to land. Take your time...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Empty rooms, Aisha? You're root-bound in too much house. So you move yourself into the smallest room, the cozy one, and close the doors on the rest. Less space, less sorrow. Start tonight.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Close the doors? Ronnie, those are her kids' rooms, not a drafty hallway!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Were her kids' rooms. Past tense. Shut those doors before they technically finish moving out, Aisha. Seal the draft, save the heat.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: They're at orientation, Ronnie. <p:0.3> They're at orientation.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Cash flow waits for no one. <p:0.3> Letter four. Big Carl, from the marina. Carl writes, very plainly, quote, my dog of fourteen years died. I have never felt anything like this. I don't know if it's okay to be this destroyed over a dog. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Carl, it is okay. It is so okay. Fourteen years is family. <p:0.3> Ronnie, please. Just this once. Be gentle.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Carl. Marina man. <p:0.3> First thing, you've gotta winterize that hull. Pull her out before the freeze, scrape the barnacles, two coats of antifoul, snug tarp. A neglected boat is a sad boat.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He didn't ask about the boat. His dog DIED, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And the dog, Carl... here's the thing. Sounds like a sizing error. Fourteen years in the same dog? Cramped. So you get a bigger dog, in a bigger pot, and you water it less. <p:0.3> Re-pot the dog.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You cannot re-pot a dog, Ronnie. That is not... a dog is not a fern.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Everything's a fern if you believe, Barry. <p:0.3> Last one tonight. This is Priya, calling on behalf of her mom. Quote, my mother is spiraling after a divorce. She's barely eating. I'm scared. I just want to know how to help someone I love through the darkest stretch of her life. End quote.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Priya. <p:0.3> Sweetheart. You being there, asking this question, that IS the help. Sit with her. Get her a doctor. Just don't leave her alone in it...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Okay, Priya, easy fix. Your mother is root-bound. So. Physically relocate her to a sunnier window. South-facing if you've got it. Water her less. <p:0.3> And just... see if she perks up by Thursday.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Did you just tell her to move her grieving mother to a window?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A sunny window, Barry. I'm not a monster. <p:0.3> Trim any dead growth, rotate her a quarter turn weekly so she grows even, and don't overwater. She'll bounce back.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You said that like you were reading the back of a seed packet. <p:0.3> I give up. I officially give up.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: And before we go... a follow-up. Last week's listener, Maureen, writes back. Quote, I re-potted my grief into a smaller apartment like Ronnie said. <p:0.3> Now the grief and I share a studio and it has the only window. End quote.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Sounds like it's perking up. <p:0.3> Good night.
